extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent attorneys, PTO examiners, legislators
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of statutory and rule-like standards from the manager's amendment and floor text of the Patent Reform Act of 2007 (H.R. 1908). Covers venue rules, effective date/transfer rules, search/report requirements, inequitable-conduct elements and remedies, publication timing, workplace study, severability, and related procedural changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue: substantial portion of defendant's operations
rubrics_metrics.description: "controls and that constitutes a substantial portion of the defendant’s operations;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as a basis for venue where a defendant has controls constituting a substantial portion of its operations (part of the enumerated venue provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue: foreign defendants with no U.S. subsidiary (section 1391(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: "(3) for cases involving only foreign defendants with no United States subsidiary, according to section 1391(d) of this title;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that where all defendants are foreign with no U.S. subsidiary, venue is governed by 28 U.S.C. §1391(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue: plaintiff is institution of higher education or qualifying nonprofit (plaintiff residence)
rubrics_metrics.description: "(4) where the plaintiff resides, if the plaintiff is— (A) an institution of higher education as defined under section 101(a) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. section 1001(a)); or (B) a nonprofit organization that— (i) is described in section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986; (ii) is exempt from taxation under section 501(a) of such Code; and (iii) serves primarily as the patent and licensing organization for an institution of higher education as defined under section 101(a) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1001(a));"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows venue where the plaintiff resides when the plaintiff is a university (per Higher Education Act) or a qualifying nonprofit patent/licensing organization (501(c)(3), tax-exempt, primarily serves a university).

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue: plaintiff/subsidiary place of business engaged in substantial R&D/manufacturing/management activities
rubrics_metrics.description: "(5) where the plaintiff or a subsidiary has a place of business that is engaged in substantial— (A) research and development, (B) manufacturing activities, or (C) management of research and development or manufacturing activities, related to the patent or patents in dispute;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides venue where plaintiff or its subsidiary maintains a place of business substantially engaged in R&D, manufacturing, or management of such activities related to the patent-in-dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue: plaintiff resides when named inventor who retains rights
rubrics_metrics.description: "(6) where the plaintiff resides if the plaintiff is named as inventor or co-inventor on the patent and has not assigned, granted, conveyed, or licensed, and is under no obligation to assign, grant, convey, or license, any rights in the patent or in enforcement of the patent, including the results of any such enforcement;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits venue where the plaintiff resides if the plaintiff is an inventor/co-inventor who still holds the patent/enforcement rights (i.e., has not assigned or obligated rights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue: where defendant has substantial evidence and witnesses (fallback)
rubrics_metrics.description: "(7) where any of the defendants has substantial evidence and witnesses if there is no other district in which the action may be brought under this section."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fallback venue basis allowing venue where defendants have substantial evidence/witnesses if no other district is proper under the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and applicability to new civil actions
rubrics_metrics.description: "(c) Effective Date.— (1) In general.—The amendments made by this section— (A) shall take effect on the date of the enactment of this Act; and (B) shall apply to any civil action commenced on or after such date of enactment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments apply as of enactment and to civil actions commenced on or after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending cases transfer rule for improper venue (post-Sept 7, 2007)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Pending cases.—Any case commenced in a United States district court on or after September 7, 2007, in which venue is improper under section 1400 of title 28, United States Code, as amended by this section, shall be transferred pursuant to section 1404 of such title, unless— (A) one or more substantive rulings on the merits, or other substantial litigation, has occurred; and (B) the court finds that transfer would not serve the interests of justice."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases begun on/after Sept 7, 2007 with improper venue under amended §1400 should be transferred under §1404 unless substantial litigation or transfer would not serve interests of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant search report: U.S. persons or U.S.-organized entity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "If the Director requires a search report to be submitted by applicants, and an applicant does not itself perform the search, the search must be performed by one or more individuals who are United States citizens or by a commercial entity that is organized under the laws of the United States or any State and employs United States citizens to perform such searches."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Director requires applicant-submitted search reports and the applicant does not perform the search, the search must be performed by U.S. citizens or by a U.S.-organized commercial entity that employs U.S. citizens to do the searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search report cannot substitute for examiner prior-art search
rubrics_metrics.description: "Any search report required by the Director may not substitute in any way for a search by an examiner of the prior art during examination."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if applicants provide search reports, examiners must still perform their own prior-art search; applicant searches do not replace examiner examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequitable conduct defense standard (clear and convincing; intent required)
rubrics_metrics.description: "One or more claims of a patent may be held to be unenforceable, or other remedy imposed under paragraph (4), for inequitable conduct only if it is established, by clear and convincing evidence, that a person with a duty of disclosure to the Office, with the intent to mislead or deceive the patent examiner, misrepresented or failed to disclose material information to the examiner during examination of the patent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inequitable conduct requires clear-and-convincing proof that a person with a duty to disclose, acting with intent to mislead/deceive the examiner, misrepresented or withheld material information during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequitable conduct: materiality standard
rubrics_metrics.description: "(A) In general.—Information is material under this section if— (i) a reasonable examiner would have made a prima facie finding of unpatentability, or maintained a finding of unpatentability, of one or more of the patent claims based on the information, and the information is not cumulative to information already of record or previously considered by the Office; or (ii) information that is otherwise material refutes or is inconsistent with a position the applicant takes in opposing a rejection of the claim or in asserting an argument of patentability."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materiality is defined either by whether a reasonable examiner would make/maintain a prima facie finding of unpatentability based on the information (non-cumulative), or whether the information refutes/inconsistently supports an applicant's asserted position on patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequitable conduct: prima facie finding test and claim construction
rubrics_metrics.description: "(B) Prima facie finding.—A prima facie finding of unpatentability under this section is shown if a reasonable examiner, based on a preponderance of the evidence, would conclude that the claim is unpatentable based on the information misrepresented or not disclosed, when that information is considered alone or in conjunction with other information or record. In determining whether there is a prima facie finding of unpatentability, each term in the claim shall be given its broadest reasonable construction consistent with the specification, and rebuttal evidence shall not be considered."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For prima facie unpatentability, use preponderance standard, give claim terms their broadest reasonable construction consistent with the specification, and do not consider rebuttal evidence in that determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequitable conduct: intent requirement (specific facts; circumstantial allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: "To prove a person with a duty of disclosure to the Office intended to mislead or deceive the examiner under paragraph (1), specific facts beyond materiality of the information misrepresented or not disclosed must be proven that establish the intent of the person to mislead or deceive the examiner by the actions of the person. ... Circumstantial evidence may be used to prove that a person had the intent to mislead or deceive the examiner under paragraph (1)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent cannot be inferred solely from materiality; specific facts showing intent to mislead/deceive must be proven, but circumstantial evidence is permissible to establish intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequitable conduct: remedies (equitable balancing and listed options)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Upon a finding of inequitable conduct, the court shall balance the equities to determine which of the following remedies to impose: (A) Denying equitable relief to the patent holder and limiting the remedy for infringement to reasonable royalties. (B) Holding the claims-in-suit, or the claims in which inequitable conduct occurred, unenforceable. (C) Holding the patent unenforceable. (D) Holding the claims of a related patent unenforceable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court must balance equities and may impose a range of remedies from denying equitable relief (limiting to reasonable royalties) up to rendering claims, the patent, or related patent claims unenforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequitable conduct: attorney/practitioner misconduct referral and preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Upon a finding of inequitable conduct, if there is evidence that the conduct is attributable to a person or persons authorized to practice before the Office, the court shall refer the matter to the Office for appropriate disciplinary action under section 32, and shall order the parties to preserve and make available to the Office any materials that may be relevant to the determination under section 32."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inequitable conduct is attributable to authorized practitioners, the court must refer for PTO disciplinary action and order preservation/making-available of relevant materials to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of time period: 180 days to 1 year
rubrics_metrics.description: "Page 69, line 17, strike '180 days' and insert '1 year'."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manager's amendment substitutes '1 year' where '180 days' previously appeared (context-specific deadline changed from 180 days to 1 year).

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC. 17: Comptroller General study on PTO workplace conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Comptroller General shall, not later than 2 years after the date of the enactment of this Act— conduct a study of workplace conditions for the examiner corps of the United States Patent and Trademark Office, including the effect, if any, of this Act and the amendments made by this Act on— (A) recruitment, retention, and promotion of employees; and (B) workload, quality assurance, and employee grievances; and submit to the Committees on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives and the Senate a report on the results of the study, including any suggestions for improving workplace conditions, together with any other recommendations that the Comptroller General has with respect to patent reexamination proceedings."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a GAO/Comptroller General study and report within 2 years addressing PTO examiner workplace effects of the Act, with suggestions/recommendations to Judiciary Committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC. 19: Severability clause
rubrics_metrics.description: "If any provision of this Act or of any amendment or repeals made by this Act, or the application of such a provision to any person or circumstance, is held to be invalid or unenforceable, the remainder of this Act and the amendments and repeals made by this Act, and the application of this Act and such amendments and repeals to any other person or circumstance, shall not be affected by such holding."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard severability provision preserving the remainder of the Act if any provision is invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manager's amendment: elimination of expansion of prior user rights and study instead
rubrics_metrics.description: Manager's amendment description: "We’ve eliminated the expansion [of prior user rights]. Instead, we’re calling for a study of the operation of prior user rights in countries where they already exist to determine their effects."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy change reported by the manager: expansion of prior user rights removed; substitute action is to commission a study of prior user rights' operation abroad to inform future policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change to discovery standard and post-grant suit protections (as described by manager)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manager's amendment description (floor explanation): "changed the discovery standard to interest of justice and ensured that a patent owner can bring a patent suit, even if a post-grant suit is instituted."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive summary from floor debate indicating procedural changes: discovery standard set to 'interest of justice' and allowance for patent owner to initiate suit notwithstanding pending post-grant proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing amendment (Issa amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Section 122(b)(2)(B)(i) is amended by striking 'published as provided in paragraph (1).' and inserting the following: 'published until the later of-- (I) three months after a second action is taken pursuant to section 132 on the application, of which notice has been given or mailed to the applicant; or (II) the date specified in paragraph (1).'."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alters publication timing so that publication occurs at the later of (A) three months after a second office action under §132 (with notice given/mailed), or (B) the existing 18-month date; designed to allow applicants time to know likely claim allowance before forced publication.
